# Ferrofin v1.4.0 against Jellyfin 12.2.0

Every graph and table of the v1.4.0 results; the summary is in the [README](../../../README.md#results).

## Speed and memory against Jellyfin

Ferrofin **v1.4.0** against **Jellyfin 12.2.0**: the median of 3 runs on one host (32 cores, 125 GiB), each server alone in its container, over the same library, 2026-10-26. One host and one library: other hardware and libraries give other numbers. Every comparable cell is drawn, the biggest speed-up first.

**12.1× faster cold start** · **2.2–4.1× the speed on 5 screens at 5 screens/s** · **2.6× lighter peak memory under load** · **2.6× lighter idle memory**

## Against the previous release

## Adopting an existing Jellyfin database

Each supported Jellyfin version and upgrade route, adopted in place by Ferrofin **v1.4.0** (commit `5112240e1923`, 2026-10-26): **13 of 14 passed**. Adoption is one-way; see [Migrating from Jellyfin](../../../README.md#migrating-from-jellyfin).

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="./adoption-dark.svg">
  <img alt="Adopting an existing Jellyfin database: every supported version and route: 13 of 14 passed; jellyfin-10.11.11-messy failed." src="./adoption.svg">
</picture>

A *path* row is a database the official Jellyfin images built along one supported upgrade route (or a fresh install); a *messy* row also carries rows long-lived databases accumulate that no API can produce; the *scale* row clones a library to about 40,000 items. *Detected as* is the Jellyfin version Ferrofin must identify the database as (releases that share a migration set share one).

## Answering like Jellyfin

The parity gate replays the **2,353** requests jellyfin-web makes against Jellyfin 12.2.0 and Ferrofin **v1.4.0** (commit `5112240e`, 2026-10-26) and compares the answers. Of the 2,307 it could compare, **1,242 are identical** and **1,051 are known differences**, each recorded in the parity ledger with the issue that tracks it, or the parity row that accepts it; **2 are filed as issues** and **12 are new**. 46 were not compared because Jellyfin itself failed them. **The parity gate did not pass** (new differences): 14 requests differ in ways the ledger does not cover yet.
